validity.recommendation: No change to Status/PipelineType/roster. Keep P6694 and P3361 as distinct rows; do not merge or drop either.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE check against the 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk family, incl. sibling P3361 (already re-audited this batch). P6694 ('Mastakh-Yakutsk III', 382km recorded, 720mm, commissioned end-2014) and P3361 ('Kysyl-Syr-Mastakh III', 84km, 700mm, commissioned 2024-12-23) are BOTH informally called the trunk's 'third line' (третья нитка) in casual Russian coverage -- real duplicate-name risk on a casual read -- but three independent, differently-dated sources confirm they are non-overlapping segments of one long-running staged project: ipng.ysn.ru (2021-03-24 parliamentary report, a named Sakhatransneftegaz official distinguishes the already-built Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk 3rd-line stretch from the still-unbuilt 84km Kysyl-Syr stretch in the same statement), Interfax-Russia via Wayback 2021-11-30 (gosduma funding vote: the still-unbuilt 84km is explicitly 'Кысыл-Сыр', separate from the already-operating Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk line), and Interfax-Russia via Wayback 2023-03-03 (Rostekhnadzor violations report, addressed to 'Участок МГ СВГКМ-Мастах-Берге-Якутск (I, II, и III нитки)', again distinguishing the then-84km-unbuilt Kysyl-Syr stretch as a separate item). These are two different physical builds of one staged 'third line' concept, a decade apart: P6694 construction began 2001, commissioned end-2014; P3361 construction began April 2022 (per its own shard), commissioned 2024-12-23. Not a duplicate; not misclassified. Keep both rows.

validity.recommendation: Re-derive LengthKnown for P6694 specifically rather than treating 382-384km as settled -- multiple sources tie 384km to the FULL, eventual 3rd-line corridor (this segment + P3361's 84km combined), not to this segment alone. Flag for a follow-up length-only search (an as-built/engineering source for just the Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk stretch) before treating 382.00 as fully confirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: Possible aggregate-vs-segment conflation. neftegaz.ru (2019-02-27) states the '3rd line, Ø720mm, commissioned end 2014' is 384km long, pairing the commissioning date with the 384km figure as if describing the same built object -- this is why 382.00 is kept as REVERIFIED in fills[] rather than blocked, not silently accepted as fully resolved. But Interfax-Russia via Wayback (2021-11-30, gosduma funding article) instead frames 384km as the 3rd line's TOTAL length 'after completion of the work' ('строительство третьей нитки началось в начале 2000-х годов, общая ее протяженность после завершения работ составит 384 км'), in a passage explicitly noting that 84km of that same 3rd line (the Kysyl-Syr stretch = P3361) remained UNBUILT as of Nov 2021 and was not completed until 2024-12-23 (per P3361's own already-staged shard, which independently and solidly sources its own length at exactly 84.00km from four separate sources). If 384km is the FULL corridor length across both segments, P6694's own built length (commissioned 2014, Mastakh-Berge-Yakutsk only) is arithmetically closer to 384-84 = ~300km, not 382-384km -- i.e. the sheet's LengthKnown may be double-counting P3361's 84km into P6694's own segment figure. neftegaz.ru's casual news-brief phrasing (which never separates out the 84km) is the likelier source of the imprecision, but this has not been independently resolved with a dedicated as-built figure for P6694 alone -- a genuine, unresolved SPEC concern, flagged for follow-up rather than asserted as a confirmed error either way.

validity.recommendation: Keep Status = operating. No sheet change; caveat recorded for future sweeps.
validity.researcher_notes: Operating status is well-supported (see fills[]), but ipng.ysn.ru (2021-03-24) records a named Sakhatransneftegaz official (Zarovnyaev) stating that as of that date the line had unfinished ancillary facilities and a working-pressure restriction on a 130km stretch (km159-289). Separately, the Rostekhnadzor Wayback article (dated 2023-03-03) reports two distinct safety violations found on this exact line (a shutoff-valve remote-control deficiency and a signage/fencing deficiency), each resulting in an administrative citation against Sakhatransneftegaz. None of this contradicts 'operating' -- the line has carried gas continuously since 2014 and is the sole gas-supply channel for central Yakutia per that same article -- but it is not a clean, fully-finished asset; it operates with known limitations and periodic regulatory findings. Recorded as a caveat, not a status change.
